before.label: Interrupt latency
before.definition: The delay between a hardware event and its interrupt handler running, plus the handler's own run time, which must fit inside a real-time sensing or control budget alongside inference.

fields.definition: The delay from an interrupt request to the start of its handler, which contributes to event-response time alongside handler execution and subsequent processing.

changes.rationale: Interrupt latency ends when the handler starts. Handler execution is a separate contribution to event-response time; the scheduling statement is conditional analytical reasoning, not a measured bound.

sources.locator: The Definition of Interrupt Latency; Interrupt Latency figure does not tell you how long it takes to carry out interrupt handling task (inspected 2026-11-04)
sources.supports: Request-to-handler-start delay excludes handler execution time. The review derives the qualified event-response budget statement from this distinction.
